rows.text: The decoder stack adds a third sub‑layer that performs multi‑head attention over the encoder’s output, whereas the encoder stack contains only self‑attention and feed‑forward sub‑layers [AIAYN:3.1:c009]. In the decoder’s self‑attention sub‑layer positions are masked so that each position can attend only to earlier positions, preserving the auto‑regressive property, while the encoder’s self‑attention allows every position to attend to all positions in the previous encoder layer [AIAYN:3.2.3:c016]. In encoder‑decoder attention layers, the queries are taken from the previous decoder layer, and the keys and values are taken from the output of the encoder [AIAYN:3.2.3:c016]. rows.text: The authors chose sinusoidal positional encodings because they hypothesized that the sinusoid functions would allow the model to easily learn to attend by relative positions, since for any fixed offset k, PE_{pos+k} can be represented as a linear function of PE_{pos} [AIAYN:3.5:c020]. They also noted that the sinusoidal version may enable extrapolation to sequence lengths longer than those seen during training [AIAYN:3.5:c020].
